clue.text: Fellow in suit pursued by a large dog

indicators.note: the jack is followed by the rest, so it comes first

parts.note: the jack is the male court card in each suit of a pack
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A man in a smart suit is being chased by a big hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal is a wild member of the canine family, a scavenging relative of the domestic hound.

clue.text: A stickler for rules, judge has battle keeping head down

indicators.note: the first letter of the battle's name drops one place lower

parts.note: Bosworth Field (1485) was the battle where Richard III died

explanation.surface: A rule-obsessed judge has a fight while keeping a low profile.
explanation.walkthrough: In BOSWORTH the head B moves down a place to give OBSWORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A jobsworth is a petty official who insists on rules, from 'more than my job's worth' to bend them.

clue.text: Keen to put on bolt and alarm unnecessarily

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to cry
to wolf food is to bolt it down

explanation.surface: Someone eager to fit a bolt sounds a needless alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry wolf is to raise a false alarm, from the fable of the shepherd boy who did so too often.

clue.text: Charming one raises cheers after slipper's fitted

indicators.note: the slipper is fitted inside
in a down answer raising reads the word upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a mule is a backless slipper; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A charming person lifts a toast once their slipper is on.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn for protection, so it is literally a thing that charms.

clue.text: A little exercise before second drink

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone does a quick bit of exercise before having another drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a single short floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms, so a small bit of a workout.

clue.text: Endless lying good for making point

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: prone means lying face down

explanation.surface: Constant lying is useful when making an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is one of the pointed tines of a fork, a sharp tip.

clue.text: Outrageous property development of mine — and Tory

indicators.note: developing the letters works them into a new form

explanation.surface: A scandalous building scheme by a mining company and a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property development' suggests real estate; the definition is the quality of being outrageous. A Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormity strictly means great wickedness or outrageousness, a property of a monstrous act.

clue.text: A pile of building waste has transformed centre for exhibiting crafts

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is changed to another

parts.note: a skipful is the load of rubble a builder's skip holds

explanation.surface: A heap of builder's rubbish has turned into a craft exhibition centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a large open container for building rubble, so a skipful is a pile of it. Its centre letter P becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful means showing craft or expertise, so someone skilful is displaying their arts.

clue.text: Shepherd's maybe upset at finding sad picture

parts.note: a shepherd's pie is one example of a pie

indicators.note: upset in a down answer turns the word upside down, reversing it

explanation.surface: A shepherd is distressed at finding a sorrowful painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is an image of the Virgin Mary mourning over the dead Christ, a scene of grief.

clue.text: Woman of 28 lifts rugby team, bringing fantastic crowds

indicators.note: lifting in a down answer reads the name upwards, reversed

parts.note: the woman's name inside 28-across is Liz
the Lions are the British and Irish touring rugby side

explanation.surface: A woman from Central America hoists a rugby team aloft, drawing huge crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Zillions is an informal word for an unimaginably vast number, so incredible multitudes.

clue.text: Grab a youth casing outlet

indicators.note: the words Grab a youth enclose the answer like a case holds its contents

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a young person who is guarding an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayou is a sluggish marshy channel, an offshoot or outflow of a river or lake in the southern US.

clue.text: I might appear on old bike I travel round on and steer

definitions.text: I might appear on old bike

indicators.note: the travelling word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: to ride is to travel on horseback or a bike
taken as written
a steer is a young bullock, an ox

explanation.surface: A cyclist on an old bike says they go round on it and steer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the answer's own voice: rust is what appears on an old bike. The second I starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is the reddish compound formed when iron corrodes, and it shows up on neglected bicycles.

clue.text: Walk-on part lacking expression associated with the stage

indicators.note: the two pieces are simply joined

parts.note: a wooden performance has no expression
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: An extra in a play has a non-speaking role and acts stiffly on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden leg is an artificial limb, literally a part of the body that a person walks on; the theatre sense is a pun.

clue.text: Mob repelling footballers when stopping goal

indicators.note: repelling pushes back, so the whole result is read backwards
the footballers block the goal by sitting inside it

parts.note: an aim is a goal
FA is the Football Association, England's governing body of football

explanation.surface: A crowd turns back defenders who are blocking the goalmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mob is a common name for organised crime, the Sicilian or American criminal syndicate.

clue.text: Collar not even reaching the ears

indicators.note: what reaches the ears is heard, so this signals a word with the same sound

parts.note: something not even is rough

explanation.surface: A collar with an uneven edge that comes up to the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is the stiff pleated frill worn round the neck in Elizabethan times.

clue.text: … yet man's OK left broke?

indicators.note: broken letters are smashed and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a man can still be fine though penniless?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and a wry question about the saying: if wealth has the power, can a man who is broke be OK?
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means wealth gives influence and power, the ironic question being whether a penniless man is still doing well.

clue.text: Got up to peer under hood, briefly lifting light source

indicators.note: in a down answer the light source sits under the other piece
lifting in a down answer reads the shortened word upwards
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a bonnet is a hood, as on a car or a hat
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to look beneath a car's bonnet with a torch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up to peer' reads like standing to look; it means raised to the peerage. BONNE turned upwards gives ENNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ennobled is to be raised to the nobility, made a lord.

clue.text: Day one of eight perhaps brings illness out of the blue

parts.note: Sun is the abbreviation for Sunday
the stroke is one of a rowing eight, the oarsman who sets the pace

explanation.surface: A day as one of a rowing crew leads to sudden illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the blue' suggests unexpected; here it means coming from the blue sky, the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunstroke is illness caused by too much exposure to the sun beating down from a clear sky.

clue.text: Be mean, withholding a drink

indicators.note: holding back a letter, so it is removed

parts.note: the mean is the average

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be stingy and not stand a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, a liquid for drinking.

clue.text: Lifts outside northern hospital department arriving out of the blue

indicators.note: the lifting word sits around the northern letter

parts.note: to heave is to lift something heavy
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Lifts arrive at a northern hospital ward unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent is a blessing that comes unexpectedly, as if dropped from the sky by providence.

clue.text: Did appropriate article on poverty involving Times

indicators.note: in a down answer the article sits on top of the rest

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the poverty word wraps round the next letter

parts.note: need is poverty
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper ran a fitting story on poverty involving The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective; it is the verb meaning seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to take it over, so annexed means seized it for oneself.

clue.text: Now, though, one can keep terminals on all the time

indicators.note: only the final letter of every one of the first four words is kept

explanation.surface: A remark that someone can leave their computer screens running constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the time' looks like a phrase meaning always, but 'all' belongs to the indicator and the definition is just 'the time', as in 'the time I missed the train'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun-like phrase, 'when' stands for the occasion: 'the day when' equals 'the occasion that'.

clue.text: Racket one used after short time producing tie-break ace

indicators.note: the racket and one come after the shortened time
short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: an hour is a time
a din is a racket, a loud noise
I is the roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tennis player's racket brings a winning ace in the tie-break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie-break ace' sounds like tennis; it means an expert at breaking out of ties and bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the great escapologist, a master at freeing himself from ropes and chains.

clue.text: Daring resistance is that coming from de Gaulle

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
que is French for that, as the French leader would say

explanation.surface: Bold resistance is what de Gaulle's Free French were known for.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué means slightly indecent, bold in a way that pushes propriety.

clue.text: Stick shrouds over vessel

indicators.note: to shroud is to cover or wrap, so the stick goes around the next letter

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A pole wrapped in cloth lies over a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a small narrow boat paddled by hand, so a kind of watercraft.

clue.text: One of the 9 people the Bill lifted getting thirty days

indicators.note: lifting in a down answer reads the letters upwards, reversed

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
June has thirty days, abbreviated Jun

explanation.surface: A member of a bayou community is jailed by the police for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bill' suggests British slang for the police; here Bill is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajuns are the French-descended people of Louisiana whose homeland is the bayou country.

clue.text: Block of fuel beside sailor turning handle

indicators.note: the sailor piece is placed next to the fuel block
turning round sends the sailor's letters backwards

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
a briquet (or briquette) is a compressed block of coal dust

explanation.surface: A sailor turns a lump of coal by its handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like the thing being turned, but it is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is informal for a person's name or nickname, and a sobriquet is a nickname.

clue.text: Uneven set for cast coming up from Inverness?

indicators.note: in a down answer coming up reads the letters upwards, reversed
the uneven, odd-numbered letters are taken

explanation.surface: A disordered stage set for a cast arriving from the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is a city in Scotland, so something from there is Scottish.

clue.text: Jack and eccentric old US expat finding place together

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: eccentric letters are off-centre, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jack and an odd elderly American living abroad discover a spot together.
explanation.definitionFit: To juxtapose is to set two things side by side, especially for comparison.

clue.text: Capital Radio listener's impression of crucial kick

indicators.note: a radio listener only hears the words, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: key means crucial and a toe is a kick with the tip of the foot

explanation.surface: A London radio station's listener gives their take on a decisive penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital Radio is a London station, which makes 'Capital' look like part of a name; it is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador.

clue.text: People pushing a little ecstasy in new drugs bust

indicators.note: the small piece of ecstasy goes inside the rearranged letters
bust means broken, so the letters are rearranged
just a little of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Dealers selling some ecstasy are caught in a fresh drugs raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushing' suggests drug pushers, but the definition means people who nudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudger gives others a gentle push with the elbow, so nudgers are people prodding someone along.

clue.text: Familiar form of female leading us through worker's state

indicators.note: the name runs through the middle of the worker

parts.note: a worker is a worker bee

parts.words: Familiar form of female leading us
parts.note: the female leading us is the Queen, Elizabeth, whose familiar short form is Liz

explanation.surface: A nickname for a woman who guides people through a labourer's country.
explanation.definitionFit: Belize is a Central American country, a sovereign nation on the Caribbean coast.
